findings: no-path-startswith-without-separator (first-ever review, new rule - correctly flags bare `x.startsWith(path.resolve/join/normalize(...))` and bare-identifier-assigned-from-such-a-call containment checks, recognizing `+ path.sep`/trailing-separator-literal/template-literal as safe). Live-grounded the full non-test actions/setup/js/**/*.cjs corpus for every `.startsWith(` call near `path.`: the codebase is highly disciplined - every live containment check already either appends `+ path.sep` / a trailing-slash literal, or uses the `path.relative()` + `relative===".."`/`relative.startsWith(".."+path.sep)`/`path.isAbsolute(relative)` idiom (examples: safe_outputs_handlers.cjs, checkout_dynamic.cjs, git_auth_helpers.cjs, runtime_import.cjs, symlink_guard.cjs, upload_artifact.cjs, mcp_server_core.cjs, create_prompt.cjs, work_queue_claim_scope.cjs, and ~20 more). Zero live misfires found for the rule's primary detection path.

no-path-startswith-without-separator theory A (PATH_METHODS = {resolve,join,normalize} omits path.dirname, a very common source of a directory value later used in a containment startsWith check): grepped every `path.dirname(` call in non-test .cjs files and every `startsWith(path.dirname(`/`dirname(...).startsWith` shape corpus-wide - the only two matches are create_pull_request.test.cjs:40 and push_to_pull_request_branch.test.cjs:35, both in test files and both comparing `path.basename(path.dirname(x))` against a literal suffix (not a containment check, and not a path.resolve/join/normalize value either way). Zero non-test grounding; real structural gap (dirname-derived values are just as prefix-unsafe as resolve/join/normalize) but currently theoretical only.

no-path-startswith-without-separator theory B (isBarePathValue only inspects the identifier's VariableDeclarator init when it is itself a CallExpression to path.resolve/join/normalize; any other initializer shape - e.g. a BinaryExpression like `path.resolve(base) + "nonSeparatorSuffix"` - is silently treated as safe/unknown rather than being checked for an actual trailing separator): searched for `path.(resolve|join|normalize)(...)+` concatenations feeding a later startsWith subject corpus-wide; found none outside the already-correct `+ path.sep`/`+ "/"` idiom the rule already recognizes. Zero live grounding for an actual unsafe-suffix variant.

durable_files.cjs:30-34 noSymlinks(file, root): a concrete, named instance of exactly the pattern this rule targets - `for (let current = file; current.startsWith(root); current = path.dirname(current))` compares against a bare `root` with no separator guard. Not flagged by the rule because `root` is a function parameter (no traceable single-def CallExpression initializer), which is a deliberate/reasonable scope limit, not a bug in the rule. Traced all 4 live call sites (durable_files.cjs:55,69,86,125) - every one passes a `file`/`bundle`/`target` value that was already validated via a separator-correct `startsWith(root + path.sep)` check or composed via path.join from such a value in `configuration()`, so the loose check is currently confounded/non-exploitable, not a live misfire. Too narrow (1 function, 4 internally-consistent call sites) to clear the established broadly-applicable-idiom filing bar used for similarly confounded findings on other rules (c.f. require-spawn-error-listener's 3-site non-filing).
